userStories.title: Critical security hardening — Keychain accessibility, biometric gate, app-switcher privacy, Apple Sign In nonce
userStories.description: As a user, I want the iOS app to resist token extraction, unauthorized physical access, and replay attacks so that my voice notes, location history, and account credentials stay private even if my device is lost, stolen, or jailbroken. acceptanceCriteria: KeychainService saves tokens with kSecAttrAccessible=kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly (not kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock) so tokens are inaccessible while locked and do not survive device migration
KeychainService sets kSecAttrSynchronizable=kCFBooleanFalse explicitly on every save to guarantee no iCloud Keychain propagation
SupabaseClient's KeychainAuthStorage applies the same accessibility + non-synchronizable attributes as KeychainService

BiometricLockService locks immediately on scenePhase=.background (eliminates the 5-minute grace window where a backgrounded app can be reopened without re-auth); the 5-minute grace still applies only when app is briefly in .inactive (notification pull-down) per Apple HIG
LociateApp overlays a blurred privacy screen (material + app icon) whenever scenePhase == .inactive OR .background so transcriptions, locations, and map content are not visible in the app switcher

AuthService.signInWithApple generates a cryptographically random 32-byte nonce, SHA256-hashes it into ASAuthorizationAppleIDRequest.nonce before presenting the credential, and forwards the raw nonce to supabase.auth.signInWithIdToken(credentials: .init(provider:.apple, idToken:, nonce:)) for server-side replay protection
The Apple Sign In nonce is generated fresh on every auth attempt and never persisted
KeychainService exposes a unit-testable saveWithAccessibility helper so future callers cannot accidentally downgrade the attribute
Typecheck passes; no regressions in SignInView Apple flow
userStories.notes: Completed 2026-04-17. KeychainService.save now routes through saveWithAccessibility using kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly + explicit kSecAttrSynchronizable=false. SupabaseClient's KeychainAuthStorage mirrors the same two attributes. BiometricLockService.recordBackgroundTransition clears lastAuthenticatedDate and sets isLocked=true immediately so the 5-minute grace period cannot bridge a background transition. LociateApp adds a PrivacyScreenOverlay rendered for all non-.active scene phases (covers app switcher and Control Center). SignInView generates a 32-char random nonce (SecRandomCopyBytes), SHA256-hashes it onto ASAuthorizationAppleIDRequest.nonce, and forwards the raw nonce to AuthService.signInWithApple(credential:rawNonce:) which now passes it to supabase.auth.signInWithIdToken(credentials: .init(provider:.apple, idToken:, nonce:)). userStories.title: Android: implement real sync upload in SyncWorker (currently silent data loss)
userStories.description: As a Premium Android user, I need my loci to actually reach the server. SyncWorker fetches unsynced rows and immediately marks them SYNCED without uploading anything, so paying users believe their data is backed up when nothing was ever sent.
acceptanceCriteria: SyncWorker injects SyncRepository and uploads audio to Supabase Storage then upserts the locus row via PostgREST
Sync status is only set to SYNCED after both the audio upload and the row upsert succeed
Per-locus failures mark the row as FAILED (or leave it PENDING) and do not abort the whole batch
Worker returns Result.retry() with exponential backoff on transient/network errors and Result.failure() after the attempt cap
Uploads are idempotent — re-running the worker on a partially synced batch does not duplicate rows or re-upload existing audio
The US-161 TODO and placeholder loop are removed
Unit test with a fake SyncRepository proves no row is marked SYNCED when upload throws
userStories.notes: Completed. SyncWorker now injects SyncRepository and calls uploadUnsynced() instead of looping over the pending rows and marking each one SYNCED — the old stub meant a paying user's notes never left the device while the app reported them backed up. Found and fixed two further defects that would have made the upload fail even once it was wired: SyncRepository uploaded to bucket "audio", which does not exist (005_storage_bucket.sql creates loci-audio), and used a loci/<id>/<file> object layout whose first path segment is not the user id, so the storage RLS INSERT policy would have denied every write. Path is now <userId>/<locusId>.m4a, byte-identical to the iOS AudioSyncService layout so household members across platforms resolve the same object. Audio upload sets upsert = true for idempotent retries; the row is upserted only after the audio is durable; sync status advances to SYNCED only after both succeed. A per-locus failure no longer marks the row CONFLICTED (a merge state, wrong for a network blip) and no longer aborts the batch. Retry policy is extracted as a pure SyncDecision.from(outcome, runAttemptCount) so it is unit-testable on the JVM without a Context; 9 tests cover clean pass, partial failure, thrown pass, the attempt cap, non-retryable failure, and the bucket and path contract against the iOS convention. Tests could not be executed here — the environment's network policy blocks dl.google.com so AGP is unresolvable in this container.

userStories.notes: Completed. Added AppDelegate (bridged via @UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor — SwiftUI exposes no hook for the APNs device-token callbacks, which is why nothing ever received a token) implementing didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken and didFailToRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithError, plus PushRegistrationService. registerForRemoteNotifications() is called only after notification authorization is confirmed, on scene .active. Sign-out clears the column server-side before dropping the session (afterwards there is no authenticated row to update, and a stale token keeps delivering another account's digests to the device); account deletion drops only local state since the row is already gone. userStories.title: Edge functions: implement real APNs HTTP/2 delivery
userStories.description: As a user, I need server-sent notifications to arrive. sendApnsPush() only console.logs and returns true, so the weekly digest cron reports success while delivering nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: APNs provider JWT (ES256) minted from APNS_KEY_P8/APNS_KEY_ID/APNS_TEAM_ID env vars and cached until expiry
POST to https://api.push.apple.com/3/device/<token> over HTTP/2 with apns-topic app.lociate.ios and apns-push-type alert
APNS_HOST env var selects the sandbox gateway for non-production
410 Unregistered and 400 BadDeviceToken responses clear users.apns_token instead of retrying
Transient 429/5xx responses retry with bounded exponential backoff

Missing APNs credentials degrade to a logged no-op rather than crashing the sidecar
Vitest covers token-invalidation and retry paths against a mocked HTTP client
userStories.notes: Completed. New src/lib/apns.ts replaces the console.log stub: ES256 provider JWT minted from APNS_KEY_P8/APNS_KEY_ID/APNS_TEAM_ID (signed with dsaEncoding 'ieee-p1363' so the signature is the JOSE r||s form Apple requires, not Node's default DER) and cached for 50 minutes; HTTP/2 POST to /3/device/<token> with apns-topic and apns-push-type: alert; APNS_HOST selects the sandbox gateway unless NODE_ENV=production. 410 Gone and 400 BadDeviceToken/Unregistered/DeviceTokenNotForTopic are reported as invalidToken so push-digest clears users.apns_token instead of retrying a dead token every week; 429/5xx and transport errors retry with 250/500/1000ms backoff; missing credentials degrade to a logged no-op rather than crashing the sidecar. Digest counts are now real ({sent, skipped, invalidated}). Transport is injectable, so 16 vitest cases cover the JWT shape, caching, header contract, every invalidation path, retry/backoff, and the unconfigured no-op — no live APNs connection needed. Escaped-newline PEMs are restored for single-line secret stores. APNs env vars documented in .env.example.

userStories.notes: Completed. Added migration 011_fcm_token.sql (users.fcm_token plus partial indexes on both token columns — the apns_token index never existed either, and the digest cron scans for non-null tokens). Android: firebase-messaging via the Firebase BOM, a LociateMessagingService handling onNewToken and data-only payloads, and a PushRegistrationService mirroring the iOS one — queue-on-offline, flush on sign-in and app start, clear server-side before dropping the session, drop local state on account deletion. userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need to know when the app crashes in the field. No crash reporter is wired on iOS, Android, or the edge sidecar, so a launch-day crash loop would be invisible until App Store reviews arrive.

Crash reporting on all three surfaces, each disabled cleanly by an empty DSN so a contributor or self-hosted build needs no Sentry account. iOS: sentry-cocoa added as an SPM package plus CrashReportingService, initialized in LociateApp.init() before the deferred launch work so a crash during startup is still reported; release/dist tagged as bundleId@version+build; disabled entirely in DEBUG so development crashes do not drown the production signal. userStories.title: Fix deep-link association files for both platforms
userStories.description: As a user tapping a link, I need it to open the app. The AASA file still contains the literal placeholder TEAM_ID, and Android has no assetlinks.json and no https App Links intent filter — so universal links are broken on iOS and absent on Android.
acceptanceCriteria: web/public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association has the real Team ID (or is generated at build time from a Cloudflare Pages env var)

userStories.notes: Completed. Found the scheme contract broken three ways and unified it. iOS registered no CFBundleURLSchemes at all, so the loci:// URLs the widget emitted and NavigationRouter parsed were silent no-ops; the Android manifest declared lociate://locus while its own DeepLinkValidator only accepted loci://locus, so every link the app could receive was rejected. Canonical form is now lociate://locus/{uuid} and lociate://paywall, with the loci scheme and detail host still accepted because those URLs are already baked into installed widgets and delivered notification payloads. Info.plist registers both schemes plus NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb; NavigationRouter also handles https universal links on /locus/* and /open/*; the associated-domains entitlement was added per configuration (developer mode in Debug) — without it iOS never fetches the AASA file. Android gained an autoVerify https App Links intent filter and its validator accepts both custom schemes plus the declared hosts and path prefixes, with the UUID injection guard running on every accepted route. The AASA file's literal TEAM_ID placeholder and the missing assetlinks.json are both fixed by web/scripts/generate-association-files.mjs, wired into the web build: it fails hard in production when APPLE_TEAM_ID or ANDROID_SHA256_CERT_FP is unset (verified both modes) and the generated files are gitignored so the placeholder cannot ship again. web/public/_headers serves both as application/json. Asserts private (non-shared) loci are invisible to household co-members
Asserts storage-object policies deny cross-tenant audio reads

userStories.notes: Completed. Added backend/tests/00_bootstrap.sql (recreates the Supabase-provided surface the migrations depend on — auth.users, auth.uid(), storage.buckets/objects, storage.foldername(), and the anon/authenticated/service_role roles — so the migrations apply verbatim, since a policy that only passes against a modified schema proves nothing), backend/tests/10_rls_isolation_test.sql, and scripts/run-backend-tests.sh. 26 assertions, all executed against real PostgreSQL 16 + PostGIS 3.4 and all passing: cross-household SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE denial on loci, private loci invisible to co-members, shared loci read-only to co-members, forged-ownership INSERT rejected by WITH CHECK, profile isolation (a user cannot write another's apns_token and thereby redirect their push), household and membership isolation including self-enrolment, cross-tenant storage object reads and writes, and the 008 free-tier cap (10 allowed, 11th rejected, premium lifts it, archived rows do not count). userStories.title: Android: biometric app lock for parity with iOS
userStories.description: As an Android user, I need the Face/fingerprint lock iOS offers. The androidx.biometric dependency is declared but BiometricPrompt is never used, so the setting silently does not exist on Android.
acceptanceCriteria: BiometricLockService wraps BiometricPrompt with canAuthenticate capability checks
Lock preference persisted in EncryptedSharedPreferences via SecurePreferences
Lock gate shown on cold start and on return from background past the session timeout, matching the iOS timeout
Device-credential fallback offered when no biometric is enrolled
Settings screen exposes the toggle only when hardware supports it
Unit tests cover the lock-state machine independent of the framework prompt
userStories.notes: Completed. The androidx.biometric dependency was declared but BiometricPrompt was never used, and the Settings toggle was local `remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` state that persisted nothing — so the lock the tier table and Settings screen advertised did not exist on Android. Added BiometricLockService wrapping BiometricPrompt with BIOMETRIC_WEAK|DEVICE_CREDENTIAL (a PIN is an acceptable app-lock fallback, and requiring STRONG would hide the feature on many devices), a three-state capability check so the toggle is hidden when no hardware exists and explains itself when nothing is enrolled, and a full-screen BiometricLockGate that covers the app rather than gating navigation — a navigation-level gate would still render the map behind it. MainActivity had to change from ComponentActivity to FragmentActivity, which BiometricPrompt requires. The lock decision is a pure BiometricLockState so it is testable without a device; 9 tests pin it, including that the 5-minute grace period matches iOS exactly and that backgrounding always discards it — the US-175 hardening, without which anyone who pockets a briefly-unlocked device can reopen the app. Preference persisted in EncryptedSharedPreferences; the timestamp deliberately is not, since a stored one would survive a reboot and extend the grace period.

userStories.title: Android: Glance widget for parity with the iOS Premium widget
userStories.description: As a Premium Android user, I need the nearby-loci widget. iOS has a widget target while Android has no widget at all, so the tier table promises a feature Android cannot deliver.

userStories.notes: Completed. Added a Glance widget: NearbyLociWidget with a receiver, appwidget-provider metadata sized to mirror the iOS systemSmall/systemMedium families, and the same three states as iOS (list / empty / Premium-locked with an upgrade prompt). WidgetDataSource reads Room and the last known coordinate only — a widget update that hit the network would drain battery and could stall the host launcher — and gates on tier before reading any loci, so a free-tier widget does no needless work and exposes nothing. A checksum mismatch on an already-applied file aborts with remediation rather than stacking later migrations onto an unknown schema. Verified end to end against real PostgreSQL 16 + PostGIS: fresh apply of all 10 migrations, re-run is a clean no-op, drift on an edited 004 aborts with exit 1, baseline then apply reports up to date, and an intentionally failing migration left neither a ledger row nor its partial CREATE TABLE behind. docker-compose.prod.yml's manual psql-loop instruction and LAUNCH_CHECKLIST §5 both replaced.

userStories.title: Operability: deep health checks, container healthcheck, and structured logs
userStories.description: As an operator, I need to detect a degraded backend before users do. /api/health does not verify dependencies, the Dockerfile declares no HEALTHCHECK, and logging is unstructured console output.
acceptanceCriteria: /api/health returns per-dependency status for Postgres, Redis, and Supabase Storage with an overall degraded/unhealthy rollup and a non-200 status when unhealthy
Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK probes the health endpoint; docker-compose.prod.yml declares healthcheck and depends_on conditions
Structured JSON logging with request id, route, status, and duration replaces bare console.log on request paths
Cron job outcomes are logged with counts and durations and reported to the error tracker on failure
Health endpoint leaks no secrets, versions, or connection strings
Uptime-monitor setup documented in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md
userStories.notes: Completed. Found and fixed a live container defect first: the compose healthcheck ran `curl -f http://localhost:3000/health`, which failed twice over — node:20-alpine ships no curl, and the route is mounted at /api/health. The container was therefore permanently unhealthy, which with `restart: always` means a restart loop and Traefik never routing to it. Replaced with a node-based healthcheck.mjs, declared in both the Dockerfile (HEALTHCHECK, which the image previously lacked entirely) and both compose files; verified live against a probe server that it targets /api/health and exits 0 on 200, 1 on 503, and 1 when nothing is listening. /api/health gained a Redis probe (Redis backs auth rate-limit persistence, so losing it silently degrades brute-force protection to per-instance counters) reported as `skipped` rather than `unhealthy` when unconfigured, since a single-instance deployment without Redis is valid and reporting it unhealthy would keep the container out of the load balancer forever. All four probes are now wrapped in a 3s timeout so one wedged connection cannot hang the whole check. Also fixed the probes' use of String(e), which rendered supabase-js error objects as the literal "[object Object]" — the payload and its log line told an operator nothing. New src/lib/logger.ts provides single-line JSON logging with level/msg/time/service, key-based redaction of authorization, tokens, signatures, invite codes, and transcriptions (bounded recursion depth, case-insensitive), a requestLogger emitting one line per request with a correlation id echoed as X-Request-Id and severity derived from status, an app.onError handler (an unhandled route error previously returned Hono's default 500 with no log line at all), unhandledRejection/uncaughtException handlers, and runScheduledJob wrapping all three crons so a job that throws is recorded as a failed run with duration instead of vanishing. During review I removed a try/catch from requestLogger that was unreachable — Hono resolves a thrown handler error through onError before control returns to the middleware — rather than shipping code that claims to handle something it cannot. 21 new tests (89 total in the suite, all passing, typecheck clean). Uptime-monitor setup, log-drain, and cron-verification steps documented in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md §5b.

userStories.title: Android: AI categorization and security audit log parity
userStories.description: As an Android user, I need the Premium AI categorization iOS offers, and the same security-audit visibility. Neither exists on Android, so the tier table overstates what Android delivers.
acceptanceCriteria: Android client calls the analyze-loci edge function for AI categorization, gated on Premium entitlement
Suggested categories are applied with the same confidence threshold and user-override behaviour as iOS
Security audit log records auth events, biometric unlocks, and failed login attempts locally, mirroring the iOS logger
Settings screen surfaces the audit log read-only, matching the iOS view
Offline behaviour matches iOS: categorization is deferred, never blocking a save
Unit tests cover entitlement gating and the offline-deferral path
userStories.notes: Completed. Both halves of the parity gap. AI categorization: iOS does on-device keyword matching, not a network call, so Android now mirrors that exactly — the same keyword table, the same two-match threshold, the same apostrophe-preserving tokenizer so "don't" survives as a WARNING keyword. Identical logic matters because a household would otherwise see the same note filed differently depending on who recorded it; it also means categorization works offline with nothing deferred. Suggested at save time from the final transcription (speech recognition keeps refining it, so mid-stream text would misfile), gated on Premium, and a user selection always wins — tracked with an explicit flag so a late transcription update cannot overwrite their choice. 11 tests, and all 19 category expectations were additionally verified against an independent implementation. Security audit log: new Room entity, DAO, SecurityAuditLogger with the same nine event types and the same 1000-entry FIFO cap as iOS, wired into sign-in, sign-up, and sign-out, plus a read-only SecurityAuditLogScreen reachable from Settings. Emails are stored only as SHA-256 hashes — this table is unencrypted at the Room layer, so a plaintext address would make the safeguard a liability — and a failed write is swallowed, because audit logging must never be able to block a sign-in. DeviceInfoProvider is behind an interface so the logger is testable on the JVM; 8 tests.

userStories.title: Fix RLS infinite recursion that broke every authenticated read of loci
userStories.description: As a user, I need to be able to read my own notes. The household_members SELECT policy filtered household_members by a subquery over household_members, so PostgreSQL aborted with "infinite recursion detected in policy". Because loci_select_shared, households_select_member, and the shared-audio storage policy all subquery that table, the fault was not confined to household queries — every authenticated SELECT on public.loci failed. The app's core read path did not work against the deployed schema.
acceptanceCriteria: SECURITY DEFINER helper functions resolve the caller's household ids, owned household ids, and co-member user ids without re-entering household_members' own policy
household_members select/insert/delete, households_select_member, loci_select_shared, and storage_audio_select_shared are recreated against the helpers
Helper functions pin search_path and are executable only by authenticated and service_role, not PUBLIC
Migration is idempotent (CREATE OR REPLACE plus DROP POLICY IF EXISTS) so it is safe on an already-provisioned database
The US-207 isolation suite passes with the migration applied and fails with the recursion error without it
Tenant isolation is unchanged — no policy is loosened to work around the recursion
userStories.notes: Completed. Added backend/migrations/010_fix_rls_recursion.sql with current_user_household_ids(), current_user_owned_household_ids(), and current_user_household_peer_ids() — all SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path, REVOKEd from PUBLIC and granted only to authenticated/service_role — and recreated the six affected policies against them. Verified against real PostgreSQL 16 + PostGIS 3.4: with the migration all 26 isolation assertions pass; with it removed the suite fails with 'infinite recursion detected in policy for relation household_members' (negative control run both ways). Confirmed the blast radius before fixing: SELECT count(*) as an authenticated user failed on public.loci, public.households, and public.household_members alike. No policy was loosened — the isolation assertions cover the same boundaries as before.

userStories.title: Android: nothing ever registered geofences, so proximity notifications never worked
userStories.description: As an Android user, I need to be notified when I return to a saved location — the app's core feature. GeofenceService.registerGeofences existed but had no callers anywhere in the codebase, and BootReceiver only logged that geofences 'will be re-registered on next app launch' while nothing on launch registered them. SyncWorker.schedulePeriodicSync was likewise never called, so background sync would never have run either. Selection also took an arbitrary 100 loci from an unsorted list.
acceptanceCriteria: Geofences are registered on cold start, after saving a locus, and after a reboot
Registration runs in a WorkManager worker so it survives process death and a reboot, not only while a ViewModel is alive
BootReceiver enqueues the worker instead of logging a comment
Selection is nearest-first, so a user with more than the 100-geofence cap monitors the closest loci
Periodic sync is actually scheduled
Selection logic is a pure function with unit tests covering the cap, ordering, archived exclusion, and the no-location fallback
userStories.notes: Completed. Found while wiring US-208's geofence tests: GeofenceService.registerGeofences had zero callers, so proximity-triggered notifications — the entire premise of the app — never fired on Android. BootReceiver's comment claimed re-registration happened 'on next app launch'; nothing on launch did it. SyncWorker.schedulePeriodicSync was also never called, so even the upload fixed in US-194 would only have run on an explicit pull-to-refresh. Added GeofenceRegistrationWorker (WorkManager, so registration survives process death and reboot — doing it only while a ViewModel is alive is how it went missing), enqueued from LociateApplication.onCreate, BootReceiver, and after each locus save. Also fixed the selection: it did `.take(MAX_GEOFENCES)` on an unsorted list, so a user with more than 100 loci monitored an arbitrary subset — notifications for loci across town, silence for the one they were standing beside. Extracted as a pure GeofenceSelection.select() with 9 unit tests. iOS was never affected because it has always sorted by distance.

userStories.title: SwiftLint gated nothing until it ran, then failed with 93 violations
userStories.description: The SwiftLint job had never executed before US-193 fixed the workflow triggers. Its first real run failed with 93 violations, 93 serious, which also skipped `Build (iOS Simulator)` and `Unit Tests` because both declare `needs: [swiftlint, xcode-project]`. The violations were not stylistic noise: 24 were force unwraps on paths that run at launch and during account deletion, and 32 were snake_case DTO properties that only worked because PostgREST happens to use the same spelling.
acceptanceCriteria: All 24 force_unwrapping violations removed without introducing an unreachable nil branch
All 32 identifier_name violations fixed by camelCase properties with explicit CodingKeys, not by widening the rule
The 5 large_tuple violations replaced with named value types
The size-rule thresholds are single-valued, so --strict enforces the limit the config actually declares
No remaining instance of any rule that fired, verified by a targeted scan
userStories.notes: Fixed by rule group. force_unwrapping: 12 sites were the same `FileManager.default.urls(for: .documentDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first!` idiom, all replaced with the non-optional `URL.documentsDirectory` (iOS 16+); `data(using: .utf8)!` became the non-failing `Data(s.utf8)`; `min()!`/`max()!` in ClusterAnnotationView became a single guard that lets the compiler enforce what the removed isEmpty check only assumed; `URL(string: BuildSecrets.supabaseURL)!` became a preconditionFailure naming the bad value. identifier_name: the loci upload/download payloads now share one LocusColumnKeys enum, because a column spelled differently on the upload and download side fails silently (PostgREST ignores unknown keys). large_tuple: HomeMapViewModel.ViewportBounds, RecordViewModel.RecordingResult, PaywallView.TierPresentation, BuildSecretsValidator.SecretCheck, WelcomeOnboardingView.WelcomePage. PaywallView.tierCard went from 9 positional parameters (six of them String, so a swapped pair would have type-checked) to one value plus four extracted subviews. deleteAccount()'s complexity came from four copies of fetch-all-and-delete; one generic deleteAllPersisted<T: PersistentModel> removed 8 decision points. HouseholdViewModel's 10 function-nested DTOs moved to file scope, which dropped its class body under 400 and both long functions under 60. Five long-copy lines carry a scoped `swiftlint:disable:next line_length` because a localization key must be a single literal and the copy alone exceeds 150 characters. Threshold change: the config declared file_length 500/800, type_body_length 400/600, function_body_length 60/100, but CI runs --strict, which promotes warnings to errors and makes the second tier unreachable — so the warning tier was silently the hard limit. Both tiers now hold the value the project had already declared as its failure point. Five view files (560-710 lines) and three view bodies (480-510) sit under those ceilings; splitting them per-screen is follow-up work. NOT VERIFIED BY COMPILATION: no Swift toolchain is available in this environment and download.swift.org is blocked by the network policy, so every change was checked by a delimiter-balance lexer over all 34 edited files plus a targeted scan for each rule that fired.

userStories.title: Android CI failed at Gradle configuration time, and local.properties was never read
userStories.description: The Android `Lint & Static Analysis` job failed on every push. The cause was not ktlint (that step is `|| true` and cannot fail); it was the US-190 Maps-key guard, written inside `buildTypes { release { } }`. That block is evaluated during configuration on every Gradle invocation, so `lintDebug` and `assembleDebug` threw too, and `Build & Test` was skipped via `needs: lint`. Investigating it surfaced a second, larger defect: nothing loaded `local.properties` into Gradle properties, so every `project.findProperty` call returned null regardless of what scripts/generate-secrets.sh wrote.
acceptanceCriteria: lintDebug and assembleDebug configure and run with no Maps key present
A release build still fails fast when the Maps key is missing, and -PallowMissingMapsKey still bypasses it
local.properties written by scripts/generate-secrets.sh actually reaches the build
Both Android CI jobs generate local.properties, with placeholders so a fork PR still builds
userStories.notes: The guard moved to a doFirst on preReleaseBuild/assembleRelease/bundleRelease, so it fires exactly when a shippable artifact is built and fails before packaging rather than after. Its inputs are read into plain values outside the task action so nothing captures `project` (configuration-cache safe). The second defect is the same wiring failure as note 26 in progress.txt: Gradle auto-loads gradle.properties but NOT local.properties — that file is only special to the Android SDK locator for sdk.dir. So SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, MAPS_API_KEY, CERT_PIN_HASH, CERT_BACKUP_PIN_HASH, REQUEST_SIGNING_KEY and SENTRY_DSN all silently fell back to placeholders, the release guard could never be satisfied by any value, and android-release.yml's 'Generate local.properties from secrets' step had no effect on the artifact it produced. A single `secret(name, default)` helper now resolves local.properties, then -P/gradle.properties, then the environment. NOT VERIFIED BY EXECUTION: dl.google.com is blocked by the network policy, so AGP cannot resolve and no Gradle task can run here. ktlint remains advisory (`|| true`) and its findings are still unverified.

userStories.title: Secret scanners flagged four false positives and two real password literals
userStories.description: GitGuardian failed the PR on two `Generic Password` findings, and gitleaks reported 3 leaks (4 over full history). None were real credentials, but the GitGuardian findings were real password literals — `POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres` and `PGPASSWORD: postgres` in the CI backend job — and a scanner that cries wolf gets ignored.
acceptanceCriteria: No password literal anywhere in the workflows
The backend RLS suite still passes with no password available at all
gitleaks reports zero findings over the full git history, not just the working tree
Each allowlist entry is scoped so a real credential in the same file would still be reported
userStories.notes: The password literals were deleted rather than moved to secrets: the container is ephemeral and reachable only from its own runner, so POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust removes the value instead of hiding it. Verified by running the 26-assertion RLS suite against a trust-auth PostgreSQL 16 with PGPASSWORD unset. The four gitleaks findings: `env.APNS_KEY_P8` (an environment read, not a credential), two PEM-shaped test fixtures whose body is the literal string `abc`, and a truncated JWT header in DEPLOYMENT.md. The doc line was fixed properly — `eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...` is just base64 of `{"alg":"HS256"` and said nothing useful, so it is now `<your-anon-key>`. The other three use `[[allowlists]]` with `condition = "AND"`, requiring both a path and a content regex to match; a path-only allowlist would have blinded the scanner to a real key pasted into the same file later. The old deprecated `[allowlist]` singular block had to be converted to `[[allowlists]]` because gitleaks refuses to load a config mixing the two. Verified with gitleaks 8.28.0 against all 95 commits and the working tree.

userStories.title: The iOS build and the Android Kotlin compile had never actually run
userStories.description: Fixing SwiftLint and the Gradle configuration failure let two jobs execute for the very first time, and both failed immediately on defects that had been invisible. `Build (iOS Simulator)` had always been skipped via `needs: [swiftlint, xcode-project]`; the Android lint job had always died before `compileDebugKotlin`.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/generate-secrets.sh runs on the bash 3.2 that macos-14 provides
A missing variable is named in the error output instead of producing an empty list
BuildSecrets.swift is in the app target even though it is gitignored, and --check gives the same answer whether or not it has been generated
The Android debug variant compiles: no unresolved references, no argument type mismatches
A release build still refuses to ship without certificate pinning
userStories.notes: Four separate defects, each masked by the job that never ran. (1) `check_vars` used `local -n`, a bash 4.3 nameref; macos-14's /bin/bash is 3.2, so it failed with "local: -n: invalid option" and then reported an EMPTY list of missing variables — the error named nothing. Now takes the names as "$@". (2) CERT_PIN_HASH was in ios_required while ci.yml deliberately exports it empty, so the iOS build could never pass. An empty pin has a defined meaning (pinning off), which is why BuildSecretsValidator classes it non-critical and the Android list omits it — so it is optional now, and release.yml/testflight.yml assert it explicitly, which is where shipping without pinning actually matters. Those two workflows also switched from bare (auto) mode to --ios: in auto mode a missing iOS secret is only a skipped platform, which would have left BuildSecrets.swift ungenerated and failed later as a confusing compile error. (3) The generated pbxproj had ZERO references to BuildSecrets.swift, because the generator walks the filesystem and that file is gitignored — so the build would have failed at every `BuildSecrets.` use site with "cannot find 'BuildSecrets' in scope". An ALWAYS_APP_SOURCES list now declares it unconditionally, which also makes --check deterministic rather than dependent on whether the developer has generated their secrets. (4) The first-ever Kotlin compile produced 9 errors: `auth.retrieveUser()` needs a JWT (the no-argument form is `retrieveUserForCurrentSession`); `SupabaseClientProvider.client` was accessed statically on an injected @Singleton class in HouseholdViewModel, the only place in the codebase doing so — AuthRepository, SyncRepository and PushRegistrationService all inject it — and that error type masked a missing `io.github.jan.supabase.auth.auth` import in the same file; and NearbyLociWidget imported `androidx.glance.action.actionStartActivity`, which only offers reified-Activity and ComponentName forms, neither able to carry a deep link. The Intent overload is in androidx.glance.appwidget.action — verified by reading the Glance source from the androidx GitHub mirror, since dl.google.com is blocked here and the artifacts cannot be fetched.
